# Acts of Thomas — Chapter 4
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Source:** Syriac MS / Greek recension, Acts of Thomas 4

---

*[The king returns. The palace is missing. Gad dies, sees the palace in heaven, returns. Conversion.]*

1. After some time the king returned from the other country and inquired of his friends about the palace.

2. They said to him: "He built no palace, O king; instead he went about distributing to the poor, and he says that he has built you a palace in heaven."

3. The king was furious and ordered Thomas and Abbanes seized and thrown into prison, deliberating what kind of death to inflict on Thomas.

4. They were cast into prison.

5. The king had a brother named Gad, who fell ill and died at that time.

6. The king was greatly sorrowful over his brother, whom he loved greatly.

7. When Gad died and his body was being prepared for burial, angels took his soul and carried it up to heaven, showing him many dwelling-places there.

8. He came to a most beautiful palace and desired to dwell in it.

9. The angels said to him: "This is the palace which the Christian whom your brother imprisoned built for your brother."

10. Gad said: "I beg you, allow me to return and buy this palace from my brother, for he does not know what it is and will sell it to me."

11. They permitted him, and he returned to life.

12. When he revived, his brother was seated beside the body.

13. Gad said: "Brother — the slave you imprisoned — grant him to me, I beg you. There is something he has that I wish to purchase."

14. The king said: "What could he have left to give you?"

15. Gad said: "Bring me this slave and I will tell you what I have seen."

16. The king, astonished, ordered Thomas brought out of prison.

17. When he came, Gad fell at his feet and said: "I beg you, sell me the upper chamber of the palace you built in heaven."

18. Thomas said: "I cannot give it to you, for it belongs to your brother, for whom I built it."

19. Gad said: "Then sell it to me."

20. Thomas said: "I cannot sell it. But if your brother wishes, he may give it to you."

21. Then the king understood all that had happened, received the faith, and was baptized — together with his brother Gad.

---
*LOGOS note: Gad's return from death to negotiate a real estate transaction in heaven is one of the most inventive episodes in all of apocryphal literature. The "upper chamber" (*'aliyya*) is the finest room — Gad wants the penthouse. The theological logic is sound: charity builds heavenly dwelling.*
